title: Kenyan Tropical Fruit Salad
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Tropical Fruit Salad — a generous bowl of freshly cut mango, passion fruit, papaya, pineapple, watermelon, and banana tossed with lime juice, honey, and fresh mint. Kenya produces some of the world's finest tropical fruits — this salad celebrates all of them.
longDesc: Kenya's extraordinary tropical fruit abundance makes this the easiest and most vibrant dessert in the collection. Mango, passion fruit, papaya, pineapple, watermelon — each grown locally and at their seasonal best. The lime and honey dressing sharpens and sweetens the fruit simultaneously, and fresh mint adds the finishing lift. This is the dessert that showcases what Kenya naturally does better than almost anywhere else.
ingredients: 1 small papaya — peeled, seeded, and diced
½ pineapple — peeled, cored, and diced
2 cups watermelon — cut into cubes, seeds removed
2 tbsp fresh mint leaves — roughly torn
steps: Prepare all fruit and place in a large bowl.
Scoop passion fruit pulp over the other fruits.
Whisk lime juice and honey together with a pinch of salt.
Pour the dressing over the fruit.
Scatter fresh mint leaves over the top.
Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 30 minutes before serving.
chefTips: Use the ripest, most fragrant fruit available — quality matters enormously in a fruit salad.
Add bananas just before serving — they brown quickly.
The passion fruit pulp is the hero — its seeds add texture and its juice ties everything together.
commonMistakes: Adding bananas too early — they brown and become mushy.
Overdressing — the fruit should shine, not be swimming in dressing.
cookingScience: Lime juice's citric acid inhibits enzymatic browning in cut fruits and brightens all the flavour compounds simultaneously. The honey dissolves into the lime juice to create a balanced dressing that enhances the natural sweetness of each fruit without masking its character.
sustainabilityTips: Buy seasonal Kenyan fruit — it is fresher, cheaper, and more sustainable than imported varieties.
storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate without banana for up to 4 hours.
healthBenefits: Exceptional vitamin C content from multiple fruits.
Rich in beta-carotene from mango and papaya.
Very low in calories at only 110 kcal per serving.
culturalNote: Kenya's tropical fruit abundance is one of its greatest gifts — and this fruit salad captures the breadth and quality of what Kenyan soil, sunshine, and rain produce. It is the dessert that needs no skill to be extraordinary — only the finest local fruit.
regionalVariations: Coastal version with coconut milk drizzle.
Spiced fruit salad with cinnamon and ginger.
